output.summary: KEP-5598 proposes opportunistic batching in the kube-scheduler: a pod scheduling signature plus a batching mechanism that reuses one pod's scheduling output (a cached sorted node list) as node hints for subsequent pods with matching signatures. Status is implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: Scheduling many compatible pods is O(pods x nodes), which is slow for large jobs on large clusters. The KEP reuses filter and score results across pods that share a signature, and is limited to workloads where pods are one-pod-per-node. Review discussion moved away from a cross-cycle cache toward batch processing within a single cycle, with the signature kept as the way to identify batchable pods.

alternatives.option: Keep a cross-cycle cache of the sorted node list (the original proposal)
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers objected to the cache as an object and noted gang scheduling would deprecate it; bwsalmon: "we will remove the 'cache' and instead just process a set of pods in the same 'cycle' using the results from a single pod."

alternatives.option: Apply batching to all workloads, not only 1-pod-per-node
alternatives.why_not: Rescoring a single node is hard because normalization is node-set based; bwsalmon: "This is critical because there does not appear to be an easy way to rescore a specific node." Restriction kept for the initial version.

alternatives.option: Rely only on the future Workload API / gang scheduling for batching
alternatives.why_not: Discussion treated this as orthogonal; dom4ha argued the signature and reuse mechanisms remain useful as a foundation for gang scheduling, and the KEP is a performance improvement without dependency on the Workload API.
bwsalmon: the cache is taken before PostFilter, so "regardless of the priority, we would (correctly) get the same results from the cache."

evidence.quote: Opportunistic batching: Transparent inclusion of the batching mechanism in the scheduler to improve the performance of targeted workloads that could benefit from it.
(1) We will remove the "cache" and instead just process a set of pods in the same "cycle" using the results from a single pod.
(2) We will restrict the initial use of batching for workloads that we can confirm are 1-pod-per-node.
If the node remains feasible after adding the pod, for this KEP we will throw away the batch information and "start fresh" for the next pod.
Non-Goals * Applying this optimization to all pods. Batching is transparent but limited to signable workloads in this KEP.
